Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service New York NY
332 AM EST Tue Feb 24 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
Gale warnings have been downgraded to SCA for the local waters.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
1) Gusty winds, blowing snow, and areas of black ice into this 
morning.

2) A light snowfall is possible from a pair of frontal systems 
Wednesday and Thursday, and could lead to hazardous travel 
conditions at times.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
.KEY MESSAGE 1...

A 972 mb low continues to drive north and east into the 
Canadian Maritimes early this morning. In it's wake, weak high 
pressure builds in from the west. Winds lighten into this
afternoon as the gradient relaxes, with gusts gradually 
diminishing.

Given this, patchy areas of blowing snow persist into at least 
the morning, with a black ice potential as temperatures remain 
sub freezing through the day. Maintained the SPS in place 
regionwide until 10 am to highlight these threats.

Dry conditions prevail through the evening, and temperatures
fall back into the teens and low 20s tonight, with potential 
for black ice again.

.KEY MESSAGE 2...

Clipper low drops into the Upper Great Lakes tonight, with
attendant warm front approaching the local region from the south
and west. Ahead of it, a band of precipitation moves through 
Wed AM. Soundings indicate BL temperatures are marginal, but 
mostly supportive of snow as ptype, with still potential for rain
or a mix of rain and snow, along the coast. Accumulations 
will be on the light side, generally up to an inch or two, with
highest amounts across the interior. Conditions briefly dry out
later Wednesday morning or early afternoon. Associated cold
front moves through Thursday, and there is potential for another 
wave of low pressure to skirt the region as it slides along the 
front into Thursday night. There remains considerable
uncertainty with the placement and track of this second system,
but regardless, appears quite progressive, so any potential 
impacts appear relatively minor and brief. 

&&

.AVIATION /06Z TUESDAY THROUGH SATURDAY/...
Intense low pressure lifts up through the Canadian maritimes 
the next 24 hrs. High pressure briefly builds in this evening, 
before a clipper system approaches early Wed AM.

Generally VFR conditions this morning, with a low probability 
of MVFR cigs for KSWF/KHPN. MVFR blowing snow chances will 
continue to decrease this morning as wind gusts gradually 
subside to 20 to 25 kt with gusts becoming more occasional. NW 
wind gusts 20 to 25 kt likely mid morning thru afternoon. Light
winds and VFR conditions for this eve, increasing from the 
south 10-15ktG20-25kt towards Wed AM for coastal terminals. 

Low probability of MVFR cigs for all terminals from daybreak 
thru this afternoon with sct-bkn 030-040 cigs. VFR conditions
this evening, with potential for MVFR/IFR conds in light snow
towards daybreak.


 ...NY Metro (KEWR/KLGA/KJFK/KTEB) TAF Uncertainty... 

Low prob of MVFR cigs and occasional gusts to 20-25 kt 
developing for the morning push. VFR condition likely for eve 
push.

.OUTLOOK FOR 06Z TUESDAY THROUGH FRIDAY...

Late Tonight-Wednesday: MVFR/IFR likely with light snow likely 
developing early Wed AM. Snow may mix with rain for south 
coastal terminals Wednesday AM, before ending.

Wed aft into Thu aft- VFR

Late Thursday/Thursday Night: MVFR/IFR likely with rain/snow 
mix possible near coast with snow possible inland. 

Friday: Mainly VFR. 

Saturday: VFR.

Detailed information, including hourly TAF wind component 
forecasts, can be found at: https:/www.weather.gov/zny/n90

&&

.MARINE...
Small Craft Advisory in effect on all waters through this
morning with lingering 25 kt NW gusts. Winds lighten into the
afternoon, but oceans seas likely remain above 5 ft into late
day before briefly lowering.

Winds and seas build once again late tonight, with an extended 
period of SCA conditions then likely on the ocean Wed into Fri 
as a series of frontal systems pass through, mainly for 
hazardous seas.
